sentences.text: Shri Krishna Kant Shrivastava - Advocate for the appella  Shri Avinash Kulshrestha - Panel Lawyer for the responde Heard on I.A.No.14228/2025, which is second application under Section 389(1) of Cr.P.C. for grant of bail and suspension of remaining jail sentence on behalf of appellant No.3 Smt. Leelawati and appellant No.4 Smt. Santoshi Vishwakarma.

Both the appellants have been convicted under Sections 498A, 304-B, 306 of IPC and under Section 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act and sentenced to suffer one year RI with fine of Rs.500/-, 10 years RI with fine of Rs.1000/-, 8 years RI with fine of Rs.1000/- and one year RI with fine of Rs.500/-, with usual default stipulations.
Learned counsel for both the appellants contended that the appellants have been wrongly convicted by the Trial Court on the basis of improper appreciation of evidence.
They are mother-in-law and sister-in-law of the deceased.
During trial, appellants were on bail and they did not misuse the liberty granted to them and they are in custody since 14.11.2024.
All the prosecution witnesses are interested witnesses.
There are material omissions and contradictions in the testimony of prosecution witnesses.
Deceased was not having any issue, therefore, due to frustration she has committed suicide.
Omnibus allegation has been leveled against the appellants.
Looking to old pendency of the cases for consideration, final conclusion of this appeal would take sufficiently long time.
There is a strong 2 CRA-12910-2024 case in favour of the appellants.
Hence, the execution of the remaining part of the jail sentence of the appellants be suspended till the final disposal of this appeal.
Per contra , learned counsel for the respondent/State opposes the application for suspension of sentence and prays for its rejection.

Considering all the facts and circumstances of the case, nature of the allegation levelled against the appellant and also taking note of the fact that appellants are mother-in-law and sister-in-law of the Pradeep Vishwakarma vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157691959/
1 deceased and they are in custody and final conclusion of the appeal will also take sufficiently long time, I deem it proper to suspend the remaining custodial sentence of the appellant.

sentences.text:
Accordingly, I.A. is allowed and it is directed that subject to deposit of fine amount, if not already deposited, and subject to furnishing personal bond by the appellant in the sum of Rs.75,000/-
(Rupees Seventy Five Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Trial Court, the execution of remaining custodial part of the sentence of the appellants shall remain suspended, till final disposal of this appeal.
Both the appellants after being enlarged on bail shall mark their presence before the Registry of this Court on 17.02.2026 and on all such subsequent dates, which are fixed in this behalf.
List this case for final hearing in due course.
Certified copy as per rules.
(ANIL VERMA) JUDGE (alok)
